quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 15 Questions • Passing Score 12

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help lower your chance of a crash?

options.text: Be prepared to react to hazards.

questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, you must be visible to other drivers and make your plans clear. Use proper signals and lane positioning. Keep a safe distance and watch for hazards ahead so you can react quickly. Do not rely on hoping other drivers see you.

questions.question: When is it important to flash your brake light?

options.text: There is a stop sign ahead.

questions.explanation: Flash your brake light if someone is tailgating you. The driver behind may not see the hazard that is making you slow down. Flash your brake light before slowing in places where drivers might not expect it.

questions.question: In Illinois, a person with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.1 percent is considered legally intoxicated.
questions.explanation: In Illinois, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means you are legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to drive while intoxicated.

questions.question: When it starts raining, where is the best place to ride?

options.text: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
Ride in the center portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When it rains, do not ride in the center of the lane. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left tire track is often the best choice, but this depends on traffic and conditions.

questions.question: When riding at night, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
Ride only in the left portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only in the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, use your high beam (unless following another car), use headlights ahead to help you see, and wear reflective materials. Change your lane position as needed to see well, be seen, and maintain a safe distance.

questions.question: If your rear brake locks on a dry road surface, what should you do?

options.text: Let go of the rear brake.
Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
Release the rear brake and only use the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks on a dry road, keep it locked until you stop. On a dry surface with good grip, you can control a motorcycle even with a locked rear wheel as long as the bike stays upright and goes straight.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: After at least an hour of riding.
After more than 8 hours of riding.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips under five miles. These crashes occur just a few minutes after the rider starts riding.

questions.question: Small vehicles can appear ______ and seem to be traveling ______ than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles look farther away and slower than they really are. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge where a small vehicle really is and how fast it is going.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. Is this area safe for motorcyclists?

options.text: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
Usually safe, unless it is sunny outside.
Always safe, no matter the weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip down the center of a lane. On dry roads, this area usually has enough grip for safe riding. The strip is only about two feet wide, so you can often ride to one side and still be in the center part of the lane.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what formation keeps riders close while maintaining safe distance?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps riders close while giving everyone enough space. Use single-file when going around curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway. Never ride side-by-side with another rider.

questions.question: What should passengers do?

options.text: Sit as far back on the bike as possible.

questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean when the operator leans. Sit as far forward as you can without crowding the operator. Hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What is the minimum safe following distance for a motorcycle under normal conditions?
questions.explanation: Keep at least three seconds of distance between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead. More space gives you more time to react to what other drivers do.

questions.question: Where should you place a load on a motorcycle?

options.text: On one side of the motorcycle

questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them or use saddlebags. Placing loads high on the back raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and throws off the balance. Always distribute loads equally on both sides of the motorcycle.

questions.question: How do you swerve correctly?

options.text: Press the handle grip in the direction you want to swerve.
Press the handle grip opposite to where you want to swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handle grip in the direction you want to swerve.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handle grip in the direction you want to go. To swerve left, press the left grip, then press the right to straighten out. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: What should you do as you slow down or stop?

options.text: Take the bike out of gear.

questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears with the clutch as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear when stopped so you can move quickly if needed.
